**3B.4 Research Note: Bongbong Marcos in 2024**

**Working judgment:** `Partial / limited yes`. Marcos’s administration took some real but narrow steps toward due process and investigation, especially on drug-war killings and POGO-linked abuse. I did not find strong evidence of a durable, independent complaint/oversight system that clearly reached politically protected actors or consistently translated into accountability.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Positive | 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Philippines | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128580.html | The report says the Marcos administration shifted the antidrug campaign toward treatment, due process, and rule-of-law investigations. This is the clearest official indication of a due-process orientation. | 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| Positive | DOJ creates task force to review EJK cases | Philippine News Agency | 2024-11-06 | https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1237266 | The DOJ created a task force to investigate extrajudicial killings, build cases, and file charges if warranted. This is the strongest 2024 example of an abuse-investigation mechanism. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Positive | No PH cooperation with ICC unless PRRD wants it - PBBM | Presidential Communications Office | 2024-11-14 | https://pco.gov.ph/news_releases/no-ph-cooperation-with-icc-unless-prrd-wants-it-pbbm/ | Marcos said domestic authorities would keep reviewing the drug-war record and the DOJ would continue reassessing testimonies and evidence. This shows some internal review capacity, though it is weakened by his refusal to cooperate with the ICC. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Positive | Marcos bans POGOs, cites disorder it caused PH | Philippine Daily Inquirer | 2024-07-23 | https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1964063/marcos-bans-pogo-cites-disorder-it-caused-ph | Marcos banned POGOs after citing torture, kidnapping, trafficking, and murder tied to the sector. This is a concrete action against a tolerated abuse ecosystem, though not a general oversight reform. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Positive | Marcos announces ban on all POGO | GMA News Online | 2024-07-22 | https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/nation/914272/marcos-announces-ban-on-all-pogo/story/ | The ban was framed as stopping “grave abuse” and illegal acts and winding the industry down. This supports the view that Marcos sometimes acted against abusive networks rather than protecting them. | 3B.4, 3B.2 |
| Negative | World Report 2025: Philippines | Human Rights Watch | 2025-01-16 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/philippines | HRW says drug-war killings persisted in 2024, disappearances continued, and the Marcos administration still refused ICC cooperation. This is strong evidence that accountability mechanisms remained incomplete and ineffective. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: “Submit and surrender”: the harms of arbitrary drug detention in the Philippines | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa35/8759/2024/en/ | Amnesty documents torture, ill-treatment, arbitrary detention, and coerced or unreliable confessions in drug “rehabilitation” settings. This indicates abuse persisted despite nominal due-process language. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: “Red-Tagging” Puts Activists at Risk | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/philippines-red-tagging-puts-activists-risk | HRW says red-tagging under Marcos put activists at serious risk and involved officials/supporters accusing critics of insurgent ties. That undercuts any claim of effective complaint handling or protection from politically protected actors. | 3B.4, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Philippines: Dangerous “Red Tagging” of Labor Leaders | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-25 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/25/philippines-dangerous-red-tagging-labor-leaders | HRW reports officials and police or military members repeatedly visited and threatened union leaders by linking them to communism. This is strong evidence of tolerated intimidation with weak independent remedy. | 3B.4, 3B.3, 3B.2 |
| Mixed / negative | Philippines | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/philippines | The report notes red-tagging, libel pressure, blocked sites, and threats to journalists persisted under Marcos. That suggests a still-coercive environment, even if not a direct account of complaint-system failure. | 3B.4, 3B.3, 3B.2 |

**Synthesis**
- Marcos did build or use some accountability channels in 2024, especially the DOJ EJK task force and internal review of the drug war record.
- He also took a real action against an abusive non-state network with the POGO ban.
- But the broader record still shows weak protection against abuse by security-adjacent or politically protected actors, especially through red-tagging, intimidation, and the persistence of drug-war harms.
- I did not find strong 2024 evidence of a robust, independent civilian oversight architecture that clearly constrained police, military, intelligence, or allied loyalist actors.

**Search gap**
- I did not find convincing 2024 evidence of a new, durable complaint-handling or civilian oversight body with proven independence and enforcement power.
- I also did not find clear proof that Marcos consistently disciplined politically protected abusers beyond limited investigations and some high-profile reforms.
